refutations.argument: Simulate a three-player game: A loses first (say by conceding), later B and C lose at the same state-based action check. By 104.4a all players remaining lose simultaneously, so the game is a draw, yet more than one player (A, B and C) lost it. The proposed rule's first sentence ('if more than one player lost the previous game, the player who lost first ... chooses') then names A, while its second sentence and 103.1 say that in a draw the previous choice-maker chooses. The rule as worded gives two contradictory answers for a game the sources settle (a draw goes by the draw sentence of 103.1). The stipulation does not carve out games that are draws after an earlier loss, so it overrides 103.1's draw sentence in exactly the games that sentence governs, contradicting the case's own claim that it leaves the draw rule alone.

source.excerpt: If all the players remaining in a game lose simultaneously, the game is a draw.

steps.conclusion: A game in which one player lost earlier and the remaining players then lose simultaneously is a draw, although more than one player lost it, so C3's condition (more than one player lost) is met in a draw.

source.excerpt: If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.

steps.conclusion: For that draw 103.1 gives the choice to the previous choice-maker, while C3 gives it to the player who lost first, so the proposed rule contradicts 103.1's draw sentence on a game 103.1 settles.

refutations.argument: The quoted sentence of 800.4 says only that multiplayer games can continue after players have left; it says nothing about those players having lost. Leaving the game and losing are different (104.3 lists the ways to lose; 104.2c shows a team's player who 'had previously lost' can nonetheless win). So S2 does not establish that 'more than one player lost' is the ordinary multiplayer outcome, and the premise for S3's stipulation is not supported by its source. The case should have sourced losing to 104.3 and handled team games, where the first player to lose can be on the winning team.

source.excerpt: Each player on the winning team wins the game, even if one or more of those players had previously lost that game.

steps.conclusion: In a multiplayer team game the player who lost first can be a winner of the game, so 'the player who lost first' (C3, stated for any multiplayer match) can be a winner who is not 'the loser of the previous game' under 103.1; C2's claim from 800.4 about leaving does not settle who lost.
